clue.text: Produce notes about a woman, who's charming and striking

indicators.note: the singing phrase is placed round the charming woman, so about signals one piece wrapping the other

parts.note: to produce musical notes is to sing
a woman who casts charms or spells is a witch

explanation.surface: Someone who sings about a captivating, striking woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charming' looks like praise for the woman but belongs to the witch, and 'striking' is the definition in its sense of hitting, not of looking impressive.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitting someone with a thin cane or whip is beating them, so a striking blow is a lashing one.

clue.text: Paper-seller taking a place with some hesitation

parts.note: a station is a place or post, as in a railway or police station
er is the sound of a speaker hesitating

explanation.surface: A newsagent takes over a site, though a little hesitantly.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop selling writing paper, envelopes and pens is the trade of a stationer.

clue.text: One wise man has got a copy

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
a mage is a learned magician or wise man, like the Magi

explanation.surface: One of the Magi has a duplicate.
explanation.definitionFit: A likeness or replica of something is its image, as in the very picture of his father.

clue.text: A minister's frugal tea?

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
a frugal meal is a plain one, with no frills

explanation.surface: A clergyman's modest afternoon cuppa.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a whimsical split of the answer into two everyday words; 'frugal' comes first in the clue but its piece goes second, and 'A minister's' stands for 'a minister is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman attached to a regiment, college or hospital is a kind of minister of religion.

clue.text: New form of travel in space

indicators.note: a new form of the words means their letters are remade in another order

explanation.surface: A novel way of journeying through outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New form of' rearranges TRAVEL and IN; 'space' is not the cosmos but a gap of time or distance.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap or pause between two events is an interval, a stretch of time or room.

clue.text: In old age dress up — a belt or sash is what's needed

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the pieces are read from the bottom, so they come out backwards

parts.note: eld is an archaic word for old age
to rig someone out is to dress them

explanation.surface: Elderly people dressing up need a belt or sash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the whole run ELDRIG (ELD then RIG) backwards; 'In' and 'is what's needed' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A girdle is a band worn round the waist, so a belt or sash is an example of one.

clue.text: Underwear nobody wants to make

explanation.surface: Underwear that no one wants to make.
explanation.definitionFit: Petticoats worn under a dress are one sense; mistakes or errors are the other, which nobody wants to commit.

clue.text: Look round about tea-time or go hungry

indicators.note: the looking word goes round the time, so round signals one piece enclosing another

parts.note: to look fixedly is to stare
traditional British tea-time is about five o'clock, and V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Glance around near tea-time, or else go without food.
explanation.walkthrough: British afternoon tea was traditionally taken at around five o'clock, hence V.
explanation.definitionFit: To be without food for a long time is to starve, the extreme of going hungry.

clue.text: There could be seven in it, but that would be crowded

indicators.note: these words say the following letters could become something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Seven people could fit in it, but that would be a squeeze.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is a link; 'There could be' rearranges SEVEN, IN and IT. Intensive farming packs animals together, so it is crowded.
explanation.definitionFit: Intensive farming or housing concentrates many in a small space, so it is densely packed.

clue.text: River sport

explanation.surface: A river used for sporting activity.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spree is the river through Berlin; a spree is also a lively frolic or bout of fun, an old sense of sport.

clue.text: Getting mad at an eccentric — so inflexible

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are set in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Becoming angry at an odd person, and refusing to bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' looks like the person being shouted at, but it is the signal to rearrange MAD, AT and AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unbending in opinion is adamant, refusing to be moved.

clue.text: Being an engineer, he has parts for the power supply

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
an actor is a man who has parts in plays

explanation.surface: An engineer who also takes roles keeps the power on.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear plant's core generating electricity is a reactor, a source of energy for the grid.

clue.text: Absolutely perfect, thought the novice

parts.note: a thought is an idea
L is for learner, the plate a British learner driver displays

explanation.surface: The beginner believed it was flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flawless and exactly as wished for is ideal, a model of excellence.

clue.text: This bearing must be to the point

definitions.text: This bearing must be to the point

parts.words: This bearing must be to the point
parts.note: bearing here is the connection one matter has on another, and a remark that bears on the matter is to the point

explanation.surface: A compass bearing that has to aim at the target.
explanation.definitionFit: Pertinence, or bearing on the matter in hand, is what being to the point means.

clue.text: A cult in a new union of seamen

indicators.note: a new union of the letters joins them together in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A sect joins a new trade union for sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new union' looks like a trade union for sailors but rearranges A CULT IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything to do with sailors, ships or navigation is nautical, relating to seafaring.

clue.text: Bold woman remains in retirement

parts.note: Una is a woman's name

indicators.note: the remains are placed inside the word for retirement

parts.note: retiring for the night means going to bed
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A brazen woman stays put after she retires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' is going to bed, not leaving work; 'remains' is the noun ASH, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Unembarrassed and shameless conduct is unabashed, which is bold behaviour.

clue.text: The record in greatest demand is "Carmen"

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, across the word breaks

explanation.surface: The most popular recording is the opera Carmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'greatest' only completes the picture of a chart topper; the letters run from the end of 'demand' through 'is' into 'Carmen'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gramophone record is a flat disc that is played.

clue.text: Whip a fellow taking the painter from a boat

parts.note: the cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip, called the cat for short

indicators.note: the fellow takes in the painter, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a man is a fellow
RA stands for Royal Academician, a painter elected to the Royal Academy

explanation.surface: Lash a man who unties the mooring rope from a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: A painter is also a boat's mooring rope, which suits the surface but here is RA, the artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin-hulled sailing vessel is a catamaran, a type of boat.

clue.text: Can survive without quarters, as may be seen

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the survival word goes round the quarters

parts.note: something viable is able to survive
E and W are east and west, two quarters or points of the compass

explanation.surface: Able to live without lodgings, as you can see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking but means outside: VIABLE surrounds EW.
explanation.definitionFit: Something visible or able to be watched is viewable, open to being looked at.

clue.text: Go on and stop a swimmer in the main

parts.note: to harp on is to keep going on about something
to seal a gap is to stop it up

explanation.surface: Keep nagging and put a stopper on a creature swimming at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the open sea, an old poetic term.
explanation.definitionFit: A species of seal found in the North Atlantic, a marine mammal that swims in the ocean.

clue.text: Study in Scarlet? A character therein

indicators.note: therein places the letter inside the colour word just given

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red
a character is a letter, here the letter A

explanation.surface: The Sherlock Holmes novel A Study in Scarlet, with a character inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Conan Doyle's A Study in Scarlet; 'Study' is the definition, as in reading a subject at university.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a subject at a British university is to study it.

clue.text: Light thread

parts.note: a fine wire that glows inside a bulb, a thread that gives light

explanation.surface: A fine strand of yarn.
explanation.definitionFit: The glowing wire inside an incandescent bulb is a fine strand that gives illumination.

clue.text: The nurse has to be compassionate

explanation.surface: Nurses must be kind and caring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to be' is a link; the first sense is one who tends, as a nurse tends patients.
explanation.definitionFit: One who tends or looks after someone is a carer; kind and gentle feeling is the other sense.

clue.text: Picture a man bound up with business

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading from the bottom, so the bound man runs backwards

parts.note: a serf was a man bound to the land of his lord
Co is short for company, a business

explanation.surface: Imagine a man tied up in work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SERF to make FRES; 'Picture' is the noun, a painting, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting done on wet plaster is a fresco, a kind of mural picture.

clue.text: Shabby fellow given a fright — and the bird

parts.note: a scare is a fright
a crow is a black bird

explanation.surface: A ragged man is startled, and so is the bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a field figure frightening birds; the definition is its other sense, a scruffy-looking person.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaunt, ragged-looking person is called a scarecrow from the stuffed figure in old clothes.

clue.text: Two ways to get staff

parts.note: St is short for street, one kind of way
Ave is short for avenue, another kind of way

explanation.surface: Two methods of getting employees.
explanation.definitionFit: A stout stick or pole is a stave, as is a staff.

clue.text: Punctilious about universal Jewish holiday

indicators.note: the punctilious word goes round the universal letter, so about signals enclosure

parts.note: someone prim is stiffly punctilious about propriety
U is the British film rating for universal, suitable for all

explanation.surface: Being fussy about a Jewish festival that everyone keeps.
explanation.definitionFit: The festival commemorating Esther's rescue of the Jews in Persia is a holiday of the Jewish calendar.

clue.text: Gathered together when so inclined

explanation.surface: Collected up when feeling like it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when so' is a link; a raked stage slopes towards the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaves pulled into a pile with a garden tool were collected; a sloping stage or mast is at an angle.

clue.text: A copper provides cover for such pests

parts.note: a copper is a penny coin, abbreviated p
to hide something is to provide cover for it

explanation.surface: A policeman protects such pests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is a penny, P.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly and blackfly are plant lice that damage crops, a plural of the insect name.

clue.text: A Luddite wave?

explanation.surface: A gesture from a machine-wrecking protester.
explanation.walkthrough: The Luddites were early nineteenth-century English workers who smashed machinery; one was a machine breaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A Luddite smashed machinery, so was a wrecker of looms; a large wave crashing on shore is the other sense.

clue.text: Foreign articles found in a wood

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
der is the German word for the

explanation.surface: Overseas goods discovered in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' are grammatical words for the, not goods.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder is a shrub or small tree, whose timber is a kind of wood.

clue.text: Having too much on, even a lord can break down.

indicators.note: breaking down the words means taking them apart and rebuilding them in a new order

explanation.surface: Overburdened, even a nobleman may collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can break down' looks like the lord collapsing but rearranges EVEN A LORD.
explanation.definitionFit: Being loaded with too heavy a burden is being overladen.
